skill.name: fix-my-last-line
skill.description: Review tweet endings by testing deletion first, identifying the final line's purpose, and retaining meaningful turns, rhythm, or genuine questions.
skill.summary: Remove unnecessary tweet endings while preserving lines that add meaning.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.value_statement: Unnecessary final lines can weaken an otherwise clear tweet. This skill tests deletion first and keeps endings that contribute meaning, rhythm, or a genuine question.
actual_capabilities: Compare a tweet with and without its final line before proposing further edits.
Identify endings that explain a joke, hedge, soften, request engagement, introduce a turn, or establish rhythm.
Retain endings that create a meaningful turn, support a thread, or ask a genuine question.
Avoid follow requests, retweet requests, unnecessary closing emojis, and questions included only to attract replies.
Recommend moving truthful qualifiers earlier instead of keeping them as weak closing lines.
Describe optional VoiceMOAT tools for voice profiles, voice matching, and whole-tweet revision when a connector is available.
limitations: Focuses on tweet endings rather than comprehensive long-form editing.
Does not guarantee replies, reach, or engagement.
Includes no executable scripts or bundled VoiceMOAT connector.
Optional VoiceMOAT features require a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Remove Redundant Closing Lines
use_cases.description: An independent creator checks whether a final explanation or generic question weakens a concise tweet.

use_cases.title: Preserve a Meaningful Product Update
use_cases.description: A founder reviews a product announcement ending and retains only a useful turn, thread transition, or genuine question.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Consistent Closing Voice
use_cases.description: A social media editor reviews tweet endings and, with a connected VoiceMOAT service, checks whether they match the author's voice.

prompt_templates.title: Test the Final Line
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tweet: [tweet]. First remove the last line. If the result is equally clear or better, recommend deletion and stop.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: check whether an ending is necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Ending's Purpose
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tweet: [tweet]. Run the deletion test, then explain what the ending does only if removing it loses something.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: understand why an ending should stay.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Genuine Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tweet: [tweet]. I genuinely want to know [question]. Keep a closing question only if a stranger can answer from experience in one line.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: distinguish useful questions from engagement requests.

prompt_templates.title: Check Voice and Whole-Tweet Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tweet: [tweet]. Test deletion first. If VoiceMOAT is connected, check my Twitter voice profile and voice match before considering whole-tweet revision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review voice consistency using an available connector.

output_examples.input: Review this tweet: We removed three signup fields. More people completed signup. Thoughts?
output: Delete the final line. The update is complete without a generic request for replies.
Revised tweet: We removed three signup fields. More people completed signup.

output_examples.input: Review this tweet: We spent a month making the dashboard faster. Then we learned customers only needed the weekly email.
output: Keep the final line. It changes the meaning of the opening rather than repeating it.
Removing it would lose the contrast between the work performed and what customers needed.

output_examples.input: Review this tweet: We replaced our daily status meeting with written updates. What changed when your team tried this? I genuinely want examples.
output: Delete the final sentence. The question already communicates your interest.
Keep the question because readers can answer from their own experience.
Revised tweet: We replaced our daily status meeting with written updates. What changed when your team tried this?

best_practices: Provide the complete tweet so the final line can be judged against the opening.
State whether the ending supports a thread or asks a question you genuinely want answered.
Review deletion before requesting alternative endings, and preserve any qualifier needed for accuracy.
anti_patterns: Requesting a new closing line when the tweet already works without one.
Adding follow requests, retweet requests, or generic questions solely to generate engagement.
Assuming optional VoiceMOAT tools are available without a connected service and the required plan.

faq.question: Does the skill always delete the last line?
faq.answer: No. It tests deletion first and keeps lines that add a meaningful turn, rhythm, thread transition, or genuine question.

faq.question: Can it help with a call to action?
faq.answer: It evaluates whether the ending contributes something useful. It rejects follow requests, retweet requests, and questions added only to attract replies.

faq.question: Will it increase replies?
faq.answer: It does not promise replies or manufacture engagement. Responses depend on the audience and whether readers have something to contribute.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. The core editing process uses the supplied tweet. Optional voice features require a VoiceMOAT connector and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Can I use it for LinkedIn posts?
faq.answer: The main guidance is for tweets. The optional VoiceMOAT section distinguishes Twitter and LinkedIn voice profiles, but does not provide a LinkedIn editing workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands or publish tweets?
faq.answer: The supplied file contains editing instructions and optional tool references, not executable commands or a publishing workflow.
